relevance_note: Case report of a GFAP variant carrier with a literature table and discussion of earlier patients: "A novel de novo variant c.217A > G: p. Met73Val was found in our case by whole-exome sequencing."
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; a Python script (own scratch directory) assembled the JSON, parsed Table 1 rows, built row-segment spans, and resolved spans against the paper text (table and text use thin spaces); the script's Table 1 transcription was checked against the table. Scope: the paper's own case (proband III-1) and her tested-negative parents II-4/II-5 (sex not stated, so labels only; "healthy" parents give no specific feature, so no feature rows); previously published individuals named in the Discussion with individual-level facts ([33] two patients labelled by variant in order of mention; [27] Met73Lys girl; [13] Met73Thr girl; the juvenile Met73Arg girl, given no person-specific reference (only the group citation [13, 27-29]), labelled unnamed person 1 with source not reported; the adult-onset Met73Arg patient from "[30, 31]", labelled 'ref [30, 31] patient 2' because the Met73Ile patient mentioned first in that sentence is treated as Table 1 #16 (same reference [30], p.M73I) and gets no separate row; [35] homozygous man). Table 1 (literature table, one row per study, columns are counts; denominators are carriers per the Results) was used only for rows describing a single patient: rows with Number of carriers = 1 (2, 3, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 20), rows with Total recruited patients = 1 and carriers blank (7, 10), and row 8 (all counts blank, one variant, every feature count 1; treated as one patient, uncertain). Rows 4, 5, 6, 13, 18, 19 are group-level with several carriers and stacked (line-break-merged, unseparated) variant, protein and age cells, so they get no rows (D-31); row 1 is represented by the two [33] patients from the text, and its 2-of-2 counts (Bulbar signs, Nystagmus, Gait) were applied to both as a named-group statement; its Slurred speech count 1 and stacked ages/proteins (E72KT412I, 2633) were not assigned. Table 1 'Age' column is undefined (onset vs report age), so it was not recorded for any row. Table 1 'Other' abbreviations (SM, RFCM, RFP, H, M, M (3)) and row 7's DTR value 'B' are undefined and not recorded. Empty Table 1 cells were treated as not reported (no legend defines blanks). Table 1 '1' cells were read as the single carrier having the feature; checklist mapping: Status epilepticus/Seizures->seizures, Slurred speech->dysarthria, Nystagmus->eye movement abnormality, Palatal myoclonus->palatal tremor; Hypertonia, Bulbar signs, Atrophy, Gait, Mental retardation not mapped. Row 7 lists two variants for one patient (c.235C > T and c.*29C > T); p.R79C was assigned to c.235C > T because Table 2 gives protein NA for c.*29C > T; Table 2's ACMG column classes c.*29C > T as B (benign), recorded as authors' classification and kept (not stated as common). Proband: variant_type left not reported (paper describes an amino-acid substitution but never names the class); zygosity not stated for her; de novo from Fig. 1 legend (variant in proband, normal sequence in both parents II-4/II-5). Vomiting 'during one year after her birth' recorded as observed feature but the checklist 'recurrent vomiting' left not reported (recurrence not stated). Brainstem normal on MRI does not settle the composite 'medulla or cervical spinal cord' item. For [27], 'did not indicate any ... ataxia' excludes ataxia but not the composite checklist 'ataxia or cerebellar signs'. Ages '7-month-old'/'3-month-old' ('reported in a ... girl') recorded as age at report. publications: n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated left null (paper reports 1 own case plus 377 recruited / 212 carriers across 86 reviewed articles, no single study cohort); cites_prior_report null. Possible inconsistency in the paper: Table 1 row 5 lists 3 total recruited patients but 11 carriers.
